title: HIV neurology and opportunistic neuro-infections

steps.tx: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder encompasses asymptomatic neurocognitive impairment, mild neurocognitive disorder, and severe HIV-associated dementia, driven by productive viral infection of perivascular **macrophages** and **microglia** rather than direct neuronal infection. Activated microglia secrete neurotoxic cytokines, chemokines, and viral gp120 proteins that induce synaptodendritic injury and widespread neuronal apoptosis.
steps.say: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder encompasses asymptomatic neurocognitive impairment mild neurocognitive disorder and severe HIV-associated dementia driven by productive viral infection of perivascular macrophages and microglia rather than direct neuronal infection. Activated microglia secrete neurotoxic cytokines chemokines and viral gp120 proteins that induce synaptodendritic injury and widespread neuronal apoptosis.

left.title: Target Host Cells
points: Perivascular macrophages and brain microglia
Viral entry mediated by CD4 and CCR5 coreceptors
Release of neurotoxic viral proteins (gp120, Tat)
Absence of direct productive neuronal infection

right.title: Clinical Spectrum (HAND)
points: Asymptomatic neurocognitive impairment (ANI)
Mild neurocognitive disorder (MND)
HIV-associated dementia (HAD) with subcortical psychomotor slowing
Substantial improvement following suppressive ART

steps.tx: **Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy** is caused by opportunistic **polyomavirus** reactivation in severe immunosuppression, producing demyelinating white matter lesions that selectively involve subcortical **U-fibers** without mass effect or contrast enhancement on brain magnetic resonance imaging. Lytic infection of oligodendrocytes causes widespread myelin loss and bizarre giant astrocytes.

steps.tx: **Primary CNS lymphoma** in HIV is an aggressive **Epstein-Barr virus** driven diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that typically appears as dense periventricular or subependymal enhancing masses positive for Epstein-Barr virus DNA in cerebrospinal fluid by polymerase chain reaction. Tumor cells display intense perivascular cuffing and rapid response to high-dose methotrexate therapy.

left.title: Primary CNS Lymphoma
points: Driven by oncogenic Epstein-Barr virus infection
Periventricular, subependymal, and corpus callosum masses
Solid or thick rim enhancement with central necrosis
High CSF Epstein-Barr virus PCR diagnostic sensitivity

right.title: Therapeutic Approaches
points: Prompt initiation of combination antiretroviral therapy
High-dose intravenous methotrexate-based chemotherapy
Whole-brain radiation reserved for refractory disease
Avoidance of upfront corticosteroids prior to biopsy

steps.tx: Thallium-**201** SPECT or FDG-PET imaging differentiates hypermetabolic primary central nervous system lymphoma from hypometabolic infectious cerebral **toxoplasmosis** lesions without vascular **thrombosis** in HIV patients presenting with intracranial ring-enhancing masses. Thallium uptake reflects high tumour cell membrane pump turnover and distinguishes lymphoma from infectious granulomatous lesions.

rows: Malignant active tumour vs necrotic infection

steps.tx: Immune **reconstitution inflammatory syndrome** occurs following rapid initiation of **antiretroviral therapy**, where paradoxical clinical deterioration is driven by vigorous recovery of pathogen-specific CD**4** T-cell mediated immune responses against pre-existing opportunistic antigens throughout the central nervous system architecture in severely immunocompromised individuals.

left.title: Paradoxical IRIS
points: Occurs during treatment of known infection
Worsening fever, lymphadenopathy, and CNS lesions
Driven by rapid antigen-specific CD4 T-cell surges
Managed with adjunctive oral corticosteroid pulses

right.title: Unmasking IRIS
points: Occurs with occult, previously unrecognised infection
Exuberant inflammatory reaction unmasks subclinical bug
Immediate pathogen-specific antimicrobial therapy
Temporary continuation of ART unless CNS life-threatening

steps.tx: In patients presenting with HIV and acute **cryptococcal meningitis**, initiation of **antiretroviral therapy** is intentionally delayed for **2** to **6** weeks following induction antifungal therapy to avoid catastrophic intracranial immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome. Premature antiretroviral initiation leads to severe cerebral oedema and high intracranial pressure mortality.

steps.tx: **Cytomegalovirus** encephalitis in advanced AIDS patients with CD**4** counts below **50** cells/uL manifests as acute necrotizing ventriculoencephalitis with periventricular subependymal enhancement, managed urgently with intravenous **ganciclovir** and foscarnet. Patients present with rapidly progressive delirium, confusion, multiple cranial neuropathies, and prominent periventricular ependymal microglial nodules.

Patients present with rapidly progressive delirium confusion multiple cranial neuropathies and prominent periventricular ependymal microglial nodules.

left.title: Clinical & Radiological Signs
points: CD4 count severely depressed below 50 cells/uL
Acute delirium, confusion, and cranial neuropathies
Periventricular ependymal enhancement on MRI
Positive CMV DNA in CSF by PCR

right.title: Urgent Antiviral Regimen
points: Intravenous ganciclovir induction therapy
Synergistic combination with intravenous foscarnet
Maintenance therapy until CD4 counts rise above 100
Screening for concurrent cytomegalovirus retinitis

steps.tx: HIV distal **sensory polyneuropathy** is a symmetrical length-dependent axonal burning neuropathy that must be distinguished from toxic neuropathy caused by older nucleoside **reverse transcriptase inhibitors** like didanosine and stavudine, both characterized by severe distal burning paresthesias. Mitochondrial DNA toxicity drives nucleoside injury while macrophage neurotoxins mediate viral neuropathies.

rows: Differentiate disease from drug adverse effect
Abrupt onset weeks after initiating drug
Symptomatic relief with gabapentinoids or duloxetine
Nerve conduction studies confirm axonal pattern
